stem: Diya has the sorted scores $4$, $6$, $9$, $10$, $12$ (median $9$). She inserts the value $14$ into the list.

options.text: The new median is $9.5$, the mean of the two middle values $9$ and $10$ in the six-value list.
The median stays $9$, keeping the old middle value.
Inserting $14$ creates the earlier sorted list $4$, $6$, $9$, $10$, $12$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: After insert the sorted list is $4,6,9,10,12,14$ (even count). The median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: $(9+10)/2=9.5$.

teacher.key_rationale: Inserting above the old median into an odd-length list makes an even-length list; the new median is the mean of the two central values. Keeping 9 ignores the new count. Saying the insert creates the old list reverses the update.
